text:
lena: paging — seeing repeated CPU OOMs on tokenizer preproc pods in us-west-2, start ~12:01 UTC. Multiple evictions and node flaps. Spike looks tied to large prompt batches from a single ingestion source. tagging @josh for SRE help.

josh: on it. any customer impact visible?

lena: yes — ~8% of hosted inference requests are failing with 5xx from preproc. Error pattern: pod OOMKilled -> kubelet eviction -> restart loop.

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: Sev2 | Tokenizer preproc CPU OOMs causing pod evictions in us-west-2 | Pager: lena | Started: 2026-07-21T12:01:29Z

maria: copying the top of tokenizer logs, looks like a runaway loop in token-splitter when prompt length > 250k chars. sample: `ERROR token-splitter: allocation 4.2G failed, process killed`

tyler: which nodes affected?

josh: nodes: gke-usw2-nodepool-a-{03,05,07}. Kernel OOM not GPU. CPU saturation + cgroup limit hit.

lena: customers impacted flagged in telemetry: acct: acme-ml (high volume) — their ingestion pattern matches the spike time.

zoe: acme-ml contacted support escalate? I flagged them and sent the initial status on Slack; they said they're running a bulk migration job but didn't realize it hit the inference endpoint.

josh: immediate mitigation ideas: 1) cordon affected nodes, 2) scale down preproc replicas to reduce concurrent heavy tokens, 3) temporarily apply admission rate limit for that customer IP/client-id, 4) bump CPU request/limit for tokenizer pods? prefer lower blast radius.

maria: we should avoid bumping CPU on the same node group — it'll just move evictions. prefer rate-limit + scale horizontally to healthy nodes. Also can we enable per-request token cutoff at the proxy?

lena: putting a quick admission rule on the API gateway to reject requests with token_count > 100k and return 429 + Retry-After. pushing a policy now.

deploy-bot: POLICY DEPLOY START -> gateway/admission/token-cutoff v1 -> change-id d3f9c2

josh: while that rolls, I'm cordoning node gke-usw2-nodepool-a-03 and draining gke-usw2-nodepool-a-05 to isolate potential kernel OOM triggers. running:
```kubectl cordon gke-usw2-nodepool-a-03
kubectl drain gke-usw2-nodepool-a-05 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=60
```

lena: gateway policy in place. starting to see a drop in new heavy requests. good sign.

maria: restarting tokenizer pods with updated k8s eviction thresholds and lowered CPU limits to force faster backpressure. will also add OOMScoreAdj to token-splitter process to avoid kernel choosing it first.

josh: node cordon/drain done. restarting kubelet on node-07 as it reported kernel oom confusions.

lena: monitoring: error rate from preproc fell from 8% -> 1.3% over 6m after admission rule and drain.

zoe: notified acme-ml via support channel; they acknowledged, paused migration job. asked for timeline.

maria: found a bad regression in token-splitter introduced in last deploy: a path that attempts to allocate a contiguous buffer for concatenated prompts instead of streaming. PR ref: github.com/redwood-inference/tokenizer/pull/418. reverting that patch now.

deploy-bot: ROLLBACK START -> tokenizer-service-> image v2.9.1 -> rollback to v2.9.0 -> change-id b7a4f1

josh: after rollback and admission rule, pod restarts are healthy. no further OOMKills observed in last 12m.

lena: customer impact summary for status page: ~45 minutes degraded for subset of requests (12:01–12:46 UTC). ~8% request errors at peak, mainly for requests with token_count > 100k. Affected customer: acme-ml (bulk migration).

tyler: followups: 1) add sentinel in gateway to block >50k tokens for hosted tier by default (configurable), 2) add streaming concat path for tokenizer to avoid large contiguous allocation, 3) add an eval and a regression-test to block large-batch allocation patterns in CI, 4) improve telemetry to tag heavy callers.

maria: I filed runtime issue: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2147 (token-splitter memory regression). Assigning to @maria for fix and @eng-runtime for postmortem.

lena: handing off to oncall-sre for post-incident follow-up. I'll update the incident with timeline and RCA draft.

josh: ack. leaving channel but reachable. recommend sev2 -> postmortem within 48h and notify infra/qa.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation applied (gateway cutoff + rollback + node isolation). Status: mitigated -> monitoring. Next steps: RCA + customer communication.

lena: closing thread for active mitigation. will reopen if error rates spike again. :white_check_mark:
